title: The committee that kept the pump running
excerpt: Eighteen months after handover, the Nandur committee has not missed a single maintenance payment.
body: The first meeting ended with nobody willing to take the treasurer's job. Six months later the same committee posts a printed fee schedule at the standpost and photographs it every Monday for the project record. The quarterly maintenance fund now holds enough to replace a pump head without asking anyone outside the village. What changed was not the equipment — it was that every rupee in and out was written down where everyone could see it.

title: Reading by lamplight
excerpt: A child who entered the centre unable to read a sentence finished the term two levels above where she started.
body: She came to the centre in Balrampur at the age of nine, able to recognise letters but not to read a line. The facilitators grouped her with children at the same level rather than her age, and worked through phonics twice a week. Two terms later she read the class notice board aloud to her mother, who asked to be shown how to keep the register too.

title: The clinic that comes on Tuesday
excerpt: For eight settlements, the fortnightly van is the only place a blood pressure reading is possible.
body: The van reaches Gobindpur every other Tuesday at nine. Those who come for hypertension screening are given a card with the reading written on it and the date of the next visit. Where the reading needs follow-up, the camp nurse records the referral in the same log and the following fortnight's visit confirms whether it was completed. The log is the whole system — kept on paper on site so nothing waits for a computer.

title: Donor, recurring since 2024
excerpt: The published budget line I gave to is the same one the quarterly report reconciles against.
body: I have given to a lot of organisations that send photographs. This one sent a ledger. The budget line I chose is named in the quarterly report and reconciled against it, which is the only reason I kept giving.
quote: They sent a ledger, not just a photograph.
author: R. Sundaram

title: Volunteer, reading mentor
excerpt: I was paired with a centre within walking distance and given a rubric that told me exactly what to do.
body: I had volunteered before and spent most of my first session guessing what to teach. The induction gave me a rubric, a group of children at one level and a placement ten minutes from home.
quote: A rubric, a group, and a centre ten minutes from home.
author: Aditi Naik

title: Panchayat partner, Jalore
excerpt: Satellite cover data was published whether it flattered us or not.
body: We expected a report that made the planting look better than it was. The seasonal cover numbers were published as they came back, including the quarter that was worse than the one before.
quote: The bad quarter was published as plainly as the good one.
author: Sarpanch H. Devi
